rounds.text: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd is severely under-appreciated, trading at a compressed P/E of 4.95x [E1] compared to a sector benchmark of 15.04x [E6], alongside an EV/EBITDA of just 3.25x against a sector benchmark of 7.73x [E11]. This cheap valuation is completely disconnected from exceptional operational profitability, demonstrated by a return on capital employed of 31.74% [E10] and return on equity of 27.93% [E9], both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks. The business is generating immense cash, posting operating cash flow of Rs 2,945 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 2,045 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], which supports a generous dividend yield of 4.47% [E4] and a record total dividend of INR 62 per share [E94]. Furthermore, the company is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E38], having successfully reduced borrowings from Rs 3,117 Cr to Rs 1,964 Cr [E40]. Operational efficiency is at peak levels, evidenced by a highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT at 112% of installed capacity in fiscal 2025-26 [E89], and gross refining margins significantly outperforming Singapore benchmarks [E86]. Conceded: compounded sales and profit growth over 3 years experienced contractions of -6% [E16] and -5% [E20] respectively, and the yearly operating-margin trend is inconsistent [E32]. Nevertheless, institutional money flow remains positive with foreign holding increasing by 3.61 percentage points [E43, E45], reinforcing the fundamental strength of the investment case.

conceded: [E1] While the headline multiple looks cheap, cyclical refiners often trade at single-digit P/E ratios near the top of their earnings power, disguising the severe fragility of their cash flows. Compounded sales growth over 3 years contracted by 6% [E16] and 3-year compounded profit growth fell by 5% [E20], exposing erratic multi-year performance that belies the trailing twelve-month spike. Furthermore, the company suffered substantial foreign exchange losses of approximately INR 200 crores for the quarter and around INR 350 crores for the full year [E96]. Operations also face ongoing headwinds from logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility [E95], alongside a short-term disturbance of 30% to 40% in long-term agreements due to geopolitical issues [E97]. Historically, this name carries an extreme peak-to-trough drawdown risk of -89.2% [E54], serving as a stark reminder of the downside when refining cycles turn.

Conceded: [E16], [E20], [E96], [E97]. The bear attempts to frame a single-digit P/E of 4.95x as a cyclical trap, but this ignores massive structural profitability where return on equity hits 27.93% against a sector benchmark of 11.49% [E9], alongside an exceptional ROCE of 31.74% [E10]. While 3-year figures showed slight contraction, trailing twelve-month profit growth exploded by 2380% [E21] and sales surged 34% [E17], proving that the business is aggressively expanding its earnings power rather than exhausting a cycle. The operational strength is further underscored by achieving a record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT at 112% capacity [E89], completely overshadowing temporary geopolitical disruptions. Furthermore, fears of structural fragility are neutralized by a robust balance sheet featuring a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.18x [E38] and borrowings dropping significantly from Rs 3,117 Cr to Rs 1,964 Cr [E40]. Finally, the historical drawdown risk cited by the bear is utterly disconnected from current reality, as the company just rewarded shareholders with a record total dividend of ₹ 62 per share [E94] and boasts a stellar 4.47% dividend yield [E4].

Conceded: [E4], [E17], [E21], [E38], [E40], [E89], [E94]. The bull points to exceptional trailing metrics and record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT at 112% capacity [E89] to wave away cyclicality, yet the company's historical record features a devastating peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.2% [E54], exposing extreme vulnerability to commodity crashes. While the bull celebrates surging short-term growth and a low P/E, this ignores the deeply erratic nature of the business, highlighted by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E32, E33] and negative compounded sales and profit growth over the 3-year horizon [E16, E20]. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of operational challenges is contradicted by management's own admissions regarding severe logistical constraints, crude price volatility [E95], a short-term 30% to 40% disturbance in long-term agreements from geopolitical issues [E97], and foreign exchange losses totaling approximately INR 350 crores for the full year [E96]. Finally, the capital expenditure profile shows a significant build-up phase with capital-work-in-progress up 66.3% [E41], which introduces execution risk and potential capital drag just as sector tailwinds face headwinds.

Conceded: [E32], [E33], [E54]. The bear cites the historical -89.2% drawdown [E54] and margin inconsistencies [E32, E33], but ignores that current profitability is underpinned by structural operational outperformance, including record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT operating at 112% capacity [E89]. While 3-year figures dipped [E16, E20], the TTM performance displays massive acceleration with sales up 34% [E17], profits up 2,380% [E21], and a robust dividend yield of 4.47% backed by a total dividend of INR 62 per share [E4, E94]. The geopolitical disturbances and forex losses noted by the bear [E96, E97] are vastly outweighed by conservative financing, with gross borrowings dropping to INR 1,900 crores and debt-to-equity shrinking to 0.18x [E38, E93, E92]. Furthermore, the 66.3% increase in CWIP [E41] and execution of high-margin projects like Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS [E84] represent productive growth spend rather than a capital drag, especially with free cash flow standing at a formidable Rs 2,045 Cr [E36].

Conceded: [E89]. The bull points to record crude throughput and capacity utilization [E89], but ignores that this operating peak coincides with severe cyclical vulnerability, including an inconsistent annual and quarterly operating-margin trend [E32, E33] and a terrifying historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.2% [E54]. While the bull highlights TTM profit growth of 2,380% and a high dividend [E17, E21, E94], it glosses over the deeper multi-year contraction showing 3-year compounded sales growth at -6% and 3-year profit growth at -5% [E16, E20]. The claimed robustness from falling debt and higher free cash flow [E36, E38, E40] fails to insulate the business from external shocks, as evidenced by a full-year foreign exchange loss of approximately INR 350 crores and a 30% to 40% short-term disturbance in long-term agreements from geopolitical issues [E96, E97]. Furthermore, the 66.3% rise in CWIP [E41] and capital expenditure commitments toward projects like LOBS [E84] introduce execution risks and rising capital outlays right at the cyclical peak of the industry.

The company does not expect any maintenance and inspection in the first six months of the year, but has a scheduled maintenance and inspection close to September or October.
evidence.quote: First, reply to you , in the first 6 months, we don't see any M&I. So it may not be there. But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.

evidence.fact: The company hopes to complete its ongoing debottlenecking study in the coming year, 2026-27.
evidence.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.

evidence.fact: The company expects the normal maintenance capital expenditure for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores.
evidence.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

evidence.fact: The company feels it will be able to sustain its long-term average net GRM or cracks over a month-long period.
evidence.quote: When I look for a month average kind of a period, I feel I'll be able to sustain the long-term averages.

evidence.fact: Management noted that Motor Spirit (MS) in the southern market has a shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
evidence.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

evidence.fact: Southern market demand for Motor Spirit is projected to grow around 4% to 5% while High-Speed Diesel growth is forecast at 3%.
evidence.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

evidence.fact: The company's capital expenditure for the current year was INR 856 crores compared to INR 673 crores in the previous year.
evidence.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

evidence.fact: The company has started execution of the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project.
evidence.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

evidence.fact: The company expects a lot of commissioning from its retail outlet project in the year 2026-27.
evidence.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

evidence.fact: The company's gross refining margin for the financial year 2025-26 was $9.2 per barrel.
evidence.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for financial year 2025- '26 was $9.2 per barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel.

evidence.fact: The company's gross refining margin for the fourth quarter was $13.75 per barrel.
evidence.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

evidence.fact: The company's niche products contribute around 15% of its margins.
evidence.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

evidence.fact: The company achieved its highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity, in the financial year 2025-26.
evidence.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

evidence.fact: The company achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, representing 111% of installed capacity, in the fourth quarter.
evidence.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

evidence.fact: The company achieved its highest ever annual production of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT for petrol.
evidence.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

evidence.fact: The company's debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.18 at a gross level compared to 0.39 in the previous year.
evidence.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

evidence.fact: The company's gross borrowings are INR 1,900 crores, while net borrowings are INR 973 crores.
evidence.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

evidence.fact: The company recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, bringing the total dividend for the year to INR 62 per share.
evidence.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

evidence.fact: Logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility present challenges for the company.
evidence.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

evidence.fact: The company experienced a foreign exchange loss of approximately INR 200 crores for the quarter and around INR 350 crores for the full year.
evidence.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

evidence.fact: The company experienced a short-term disturbance of 30% to 40% in its long-term agreements due to geopolitical issues.
evidence.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company expects to see a lot of commissioning from its retail outlet project in the year 2026-27.
evidence.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): The company expects to execute its INR 2,000 crores of projects over the next two to three years.
evidence.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company hopes to complete its ongoing debottlenecking study in the coming year, 2026-27.
evidence.quote: But in the coming year, '26-'27, we hope that ongoing study will get completed.
